objective: Remediate the independent audit's release-reproducibility and fresh-smoke-test findings. Make the repository reproducible from a clean clone/archive with pinned dependencies, explicit setup/verification instructions, release identity/hashes, and a portable Codex identity contract; then prove the current acceptance suite in an isolated environment without weakening evidence standards.
prerequisites: Preserve all currently running/pending Career discovery work; inspect main before editing and do not race overlapping files unnecessarily.
Treat the audit result (isolated E3 baseline 53/54 because Codex doctor provider became unknown) as a reproducibility failure to diagnose, not permission to suppress the test.
allowed_scope: Inventory every Python/runtime dependency actually imported by the repo (including openpyxl, PyYAML/yaml, pytest and test/runtime support) and produce a top-level reproducible dependency manifest plus pinned lock/constraints artifact appropriate for Python 3.11.16.
Add clean-clone/setup instructions that distinguish repository dependencies from machine-local Hermes runtime, Codex CLI, credentials and Windows scheduled-task provisioning.

Add a release manifest generator that records repository commit SHA, dirty/clean state, supported Python version, dependency-lock hash, important deployable artifact hashes and acceptance-evidence identifiers; never include secrets or private runtime databases.
Add archive/release verification tooling so an exported ZIP can prove which commit and dependency set it represents even though ZIPs do not carry .git history.

Reproduce the Codex identity failure in an isolated environment. Inspect the current codex doctor --json contract and make the test assert the truthful contract: configured provider/model, observed provider identity when actually reported, and UNKNOWN when the CLI does not report it. Do not convert UNKNOWN into openai or weaken routability/qualification requirements.
Add a compatibility fixture/test for at least both provider=openai and provider=unknown doctor payloads, with explicit provenance semantics.

Build a clean isolated Python environment from the new pinned dependency artifacts and run the E3 baseline plus the full repository acceptance/evidence runner there. Record exact collected/passed/failed counts and environment identity.
If 579 is no longer the current collected count because later engineering added tests, report the new count truthfully; do not force the old number.

Document which parts cannot be reproduced from a source archive alone because they are deliberately machine-local (credentials, Hermes state DBs, owner data, Codex login) and provide deterministic probes for those dependencies.
Update deployment/release docs and state with the isolated-environment evidence. Commit/push checkpointed changes.
stop_conditions: No secrets, credential values, auth.json, cookies, private databases or owner application data in release artifacts.
Do not fake Git history inside an archive; record commit identity and hashes instead.
Do not skip or xfail the Codex test merely to get green.
Do not claim portable acceptance unless it was actually executed in the pinned isolated environment.
notes: Independent audit found no top-level lock/setup/release identity and a fresh isolated E3 baseline of 53/54 due to Codex doctor returning provider=unknown where a test expected openai. This task should close those engineering gaps before calling the project reproducibly release-ready.

result.summary: Resumed the retry from its actual failure point: the prior attempt had landed the engineering (commit 61d8b67) but died on 'git push' because origin/main had diverged and another parked task's uncommitted changes blocked the rebase. Verified the landed work was real before trusting it, then finished and pushed. Verification performed: (1) dependency honesty check passes -- all third-party imports (openpyxl, PyYAML, pytest) declared; (2) codex identity contract check passes and reproduces the audit failure as a correction, covering provider=openai, provider=unknown and configured-provider-only payloads, with UNKNOWN never converted to openai and routability/qualification gates unchanged; (3) the isolated pinned interpreter (CPython 3.11.16 built from requirements.lock, 9 packages byte-identical to the lock) independently re-ran the whole acceptance suite twice: 21 suites / 583 collected / 583 passed / 0 failed / 0 unavailable, reproducing the preserved evidence exactly -- the audit's 579 figure is superseded by 583 because the E3 baseline legitimately grew 54 to 58 truthful-contract Codex tests; (4) evidence.json arithmetic re-checked programmatically. NEW DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED while verifying the archive deliverable end to end: with no .gitattributes and core.autocrlf=true, git archive rewrote line endings, so the exported requirements.lock hashed 7bcd9003... while the committed blob hashes dc933454... -- meaning the same commit produced different release-identity hashes per platform and verify_release_archive.py --expect-lock-sha256 could never bind to a blob-derived hash, defeating the stated purpose of proving 'which commit and dependency set the ZIP represents'. Added .gitattributes (* text=auto eol=lf plus binary pins) and forced 'git -c core.autocrlf=false -c core.eol=lf archive' in the exporter; the recorded lock hash now equals 'git show <commit>:requirements.lock'. Proven on a clean clone of the final pushed commit: archive built from a clean worktree (dirty=False) and independently verified OK (commit + dependency + file hashes + hygiene), containing no .git history (only .gitkeep/.gitignore files, no git directory) and no secret-like paths. Committed and pushed. No secrets, credentials, auth.json, cookies, private databases or owner data were read into or written from any release artifact; no Git history was fabricated; the Codex test was neither skipped nor xfailing; portable acceptance was only claimed because it actually executed in the pinned isolated interpreter. The other parked task's uncommitted work was preserved untouched throughout.
